title: 哈克说透：加息买信誉，K型经济撕裂消费者
speaker: Patrick Harker

segments.en: Mr. Harker, David here, just to follow up on that, if inflation does not respond as much, let's put it that way to these hikes, why are they hiking interest rates there?
segments.zh: 哈克先生，我是David，接着问，如果通胀对这些加息反应没那么大，这么说吧，那他们为什么还要加息？

segments.en: I think it's credibility. Now, there will be some impact that don't get me wrong. I mean, particularly around services, so service inflation is running well above where we want to see it, but it was more of the credibility.
segments.zh: 我认为是信誉。当然会有一些影响，别误会。尤其是服务业，服务通胀远高于我们希望的水平，但更多是信誉问题。

segments.en: I mean, that the Fed had to show it was serious about getting down to 2%. It's been stuck above two for now a long time.
segments.zh: 美联储必须表明它认真对待将通胀降至2%的目标。通胀高于2%已经持续很久了。

segments.en: So I guess the other question I had was, around this debate, whether rates are restrictive enough, you know, textbook as he raised interest rates to cool demand for debt, and you look at what's happening in the credit markets, the companies can't stop borrowing money.
segments.zh: 我还有一个问题，关于利率是否足够限制性的争论。教科书上说提高利率以冷却债务需求，但看看信贷市场，企业停不下借钱。

segments.en: You look at his AI CapEx boom, you look at all the spend that's going on, and I wonder whether rates might need to go higher, if it only just to achieve the target of cooling the economy further.
segments.zh: 看看AI资本开支热潮，看看所有正在进行的支出，我怀疑利率是否需要更高，哪怕只是为了进一步冷却经济。

segments.en: So let's take two different, the consumer side, and then the CapEx you're talking about. On the CapEx, we have split it up between the AI investment, that includes electric utilities and so forth, and all else. There's not much happening in the all else.
segments.zh: 我们分两方面看，消费端和你说的资本开支。资本开支方面，我们将其分为AI相关配置，包括电力公用事业等，以及其他所有。其他所有方面没什么动静。

segments.en: It really is the AI boom, and I don't think it's going to be affected by rates growing up 50, 75 basis points. The consumer side, though, that is the tail of two cities in the United States.
segments.zh: 确实就是AI热潮，我不认为利率上升50、75个基点会影响它。但消费端，那是美国的双城记。

segments.en: That is the K-shaped economy. So the people who are invested in the market feel pretty good, they're spending. But those who aren't, they are really struggling day-to-day to get by.
segments.zh: 这就是K型经济。参与市场的人感觉不错，他们在消费。但不参与的人，真的每天都在为生计挣扎。

segments.en: I mean, the increase in inflation is really, really biting into them.
segments.zh: 通胀上升真的在严重侵蚀他们。
